hints.content:
We can map a figure onto a **similar** figure using only rigid transformations and dilations. This means the figures must have exactly the same shapes, but may have different sizes.

For triangles in particular, two triangles are similar if all of their corresponding angles are [[☃ definition 1]].

options.definition: Angles with the same measure that we can map onto each other using rigid transformations

hints.content:
Triangle $ABC$ has angle measures of $38^\circ$ and $59^\circ$. The third angle measure is therefore $180^\circ - 38^\circ - 59^\circ = 83^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Triangle A B C. Angle A is thirty-eight degrees. Angle B is fifty-nine degrees. Angle C is eighty-three degrees.

hints.content:
Triangle $QRS$ has angle measures of $90^\circ$ and $38^\circ$. The third angle measure is $180^\circ - 90^\circ - 38^\circ = 52^\circ$. 



[[☃ image 1]]

Therefore $\triangle QRS$ is not similar to $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: Triangle Q R S. Angle Q is thirty-eight degrees. Angle R is ninety degrees. Angle S is fifty-two degrees.

hints.content:
Triangle $TUV$ has angle measures of $39^\circ$ and $41^\circ$. The third angle measure is $180^\circ - 39^\circ - 41^\circ = 100^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

Therefore $\triangle TUV$ is not similar to $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: Triangle T U V. Angle V is thirty-nine degrees. Angle T is forty-one degrees. Angle U is one hundred degrees.

hints.content: In conclusion, *neither* of the triangles are similar to $\triangle ABC$.
